source.title: Prisma: An Open Source Toolkit for Mechanistic Interpretability in Vision and Video
source.authors: Sonia Joseph; Praneet Suresh; Lorenz Hufe; Edward Stevinson; Robert Graham; Yash Vadi; Danilo Bzdok; Sebastian Lapuschkin; Lee Sharkey; Blake Aaron Richards

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures how SAE reconstructions affect model cross-entropy, bearing on the loss-effect aspect of V3, but does not compare them with random errors of the same size.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are SAE-reconstruction cross-entropy values in Tables 4–6 and 9. The paper does not test linear predictability of SAE error, error norms across SAE sizes, token overlap across sizes, or matched random-error replacements. Its reported reconstruction-loss values cannot establish the V3 comparison without that random-error reference. Other toolkit, sparsity, and toy-model results do not test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: This is a toolkit paper, and none of its results test any version. It reports standard evaluation metrics (explained variance, L0, reconstruction CE, zero-ablation CE, % CE recovered) for its own released SAEs. It never measures error predictability, cross-size error behaviour, or a random-error comparison, and it does not cite or discuss SAE dark matter. The reconstruction-CE values are the study's own SAE quality metrics. With no same-norm random-error reference, they cannot show whether SAE error is pathological (V3). The observation that reconstructions sometimes lower loss is a related but different finding, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report that SAE reconstructions can lower CLIP/DINO cross-entropy. The effect is clearest for Top-K CLS-only CLIP SAEs, where it grows with depth, and it also appears in some vanilla CLIP all-patch and DINO layers. They suggest denoising but say the mechanism is unclear. They also report no significant improvement for transcoders, spatial-patch SAEs and vanilla CLS-only SAEs. Their other headline finding is that vision SAEs are much less sparse (higher L0) than language SAEs.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates vision SAE reconstructions by their effect on model cross-entropy; it does not use the original study's dark-matter error-predictability or cross-size context-overlap measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported loss effects vary by model, SAE configuration, token selection, and layer; the authors specifically distinguish Top-K CLS-only SAEs from vanilla CLS-only, spatial-patch, and transcoder results.

fits_no_version.finding: Splicing SAE reconstructions into the forward pass sometimes lowers cross-entropy below the clean model. This holds for CLIP Top-K CLS-only SAEs in layers 7–11 (down to 6.7578 vs 6.7622 at L11), several DINO vanilla layers (4–7, 10), and a few CLIP vanilla all-patch layers. The authors suggest a denoising mechanism.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In vision transformers, SAE reconstruction error can be beneficial rather than harmful to model loss in some layers and SAE configurations (a possible counterpoint to pathological-error claims, not tested against random-error baselines).

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the CVPR 2025 Workshop on Mechanistic Interpretability in Vision (MIV), Oral Presentation
record.problems: There is no same-size random-error control, so the reported reconstruction-loss changes cannot establish V3's comparative claim. No uncertainty estimates are given for these results.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 7 and 8 reconstruction-loss results for CLIP vanilla spatial-patch SAEs and CLIP Top-K transcoders were omitted to remain within the 60-row limit; the paper describes these configurations as showing no significant improvements. Table 4, Table 5, Table 6, and Table 9 results were retained.

untested.parts: Not tested: no regression of SAE error on input activations.
Not tested: no comparison of error norms or failing contexts across SAE sizes.
Not tested: no comparison of reconstruction-induced loss against random errors of equal norm.
Not tested: no split of error into linear and nonlinear parts.
Not tested: no circuit or steering analysis with versus without the error term.
Not tested: ReLU and Top-K SAEs are compared only on standard metrics, never on dark-matter size or structure.

record.verdict_notes: The reader marked this as tests/T2 for V3, but every row is an own-SAE evaluation metric with no random-error control. The paper never addresses dark matter, so I reclassified it as T6 with all rows unlinked. The rows_left_out note about Tables 7–8 is accurate. The paper text mislabels the spatial-patch table as 'Tab. 6'; the spatial-patch results are actually in Table 7.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not measure linear predictability of the SAE error vector from the input activation.
The study does not compare error norms across SAE sizes, per-token error predictability, contexts where different SAE sizes fail, or whether error persists with scale.
The study measures reconstruction effects on cross-entropy but does not compare them with random errors of the same size.
The study does not separate linearly predictable and nonlinear error or test their feature-learning properties.
The study does not test the loss of model behaviour in circuits or steering analyses when the error term is omitted.
The study does not test whether dark matter is caused by SAE training choices or shrinks under alternative architectures or end-to-end training.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-B-32
rows.operation_detail: Replaced the relevant activation with its vanilla SAE reconstruction and measured cross-entropy.
rows.note: No matched random-error comparison is reported.
rows.check: Table 4 CLIP vanilla all-patch reconstruction CE. These are the study's own SAE evaluation metrics with no random-error control, so they cannot speak to V3. Values are rounded to 3 decimals, so most differences are invisible. CLIP CE (6.762) is close to the zero-ablation value (6.908, about ln 1000), so the measure has very little dynamic range.
